name: starfield
summary: Night-sky hero running the tsParticles stars preset: 100 white points drifting at speed 0.1 with unsynced opacity animation, over a CSS star field that stands in whenever the canvas cannot.

color.description: Star fill colour. Upstream's particles.paint.fill.color.value. Set --fx-star to match so the CSS resting sky agrees.

deviations.what: MoveDirection.none and OutMode.out are written as the strings "none" and "out".
deviations.why: The preset imports both enums from @tsparticles/engine. The vendored slim bundle publishes its engine on globalThis and exports nothing, so there is no enum to import; the members are these strings and the loaded options are identical.

deviations.what: background: { color: "#000" } is dropped, so the canvas is transparent.
deviations.why: The section's CSS owns the background and draws the resting star field underneath. Painting #000 on the canvas would hide the gradient the section is designed around, and the resting state has to show through until the container loads.

deviations.what: Upstream is a preset registered on the engine and applied by name; here the options object is passed straight to engine.load().
deviations.why: A preset only exists to be looked up by name, which a single-effect module has no use for. The options object it registers is what actually configures the container, and that is what travels.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the container is never created.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. The CSS star field is the finished section, so not loading is the resting state rather than a downgrade.
